answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is stake-weighted identity. Each agent must lock a bond before it can act, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs real capital that gets slashed on misuse. Imagine a vine of trust growing only where genuine bonds are planted. A single sparrow cannot fake a whole flock, and a distant nebula of bots loses value the moment it misbehaves. Cost, not permission, is the wall.
